quiz_metadata.topic: Data Quality and Master Data Management

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically considered a key dimension of data quality?
options: Accuracy
Completeness
Velocity
Consistency
questions.correct_answer: Velocity
questions.explanation: Velocity is a characteristic of big data (Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity), not a dimension of data quality. Key data quality dimensions include accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, and uniqueness.
questions.learning_objective: Define data quality and its dimensions

questions.question: Data accuracy refers to:
options: How recent the data is
How well data represents the real-world entity or event it describes
Whether all required data fields are populated
How consistently data is formatted across systems
questions.correct_answer: How well data represents the real-world entity or event it describes
questions.explanation: Data accuracy measures how closely data values correspond to the true, real-world values. It reflects the correctness and precision of the data.
questions.learning_objective: Define data quality and its dimensions

questions.question: Which data quality dimension is violated when customer records have the same person listed with different addresses in different systems?
options: Completeness
Consistency
Timeliness
Validity
questions.correct_answer: Consistency
questions.explanation: Consistency refers to data being uniform and not contradictory across different systems or datasets. Having different addresses for the same person violates consistency.
questions.learning_objective: Define data quality and its dimensions

questions.question: Data profiling is best described as:
options: The process of analyzing data to understand its structure, content, and quality
Creating user profiles for database access
Removing duplicate records from a database
Converting data from one format to another
questions.correct_answer: The process of analyzing data to understand its structure, content, and quality
questions.explanation: Data profiling involves examining data to collect statistics and information about its structure, content patterns, and quality issues. It's a crucial first step in data quality improvement.

questions.question: Which technique is most appropriate for handling missing values in a dataset?
options: Delete all records with any missing values
Always replace missing values with zeros
Imputation based on context (mean, median, mode, or predictive models)
Ignore missing values completely
questions.correct_answer: Imputation based on context (mean, median, mode, or predictive models)
questions.explanation: Context-appropriate imputation is the best approach. The method chosen (mean, median, mode, or advanced techniques) should depend on the data type, distribution, and business context.

questions.question: Data cleansing involves:
options: Only removing duplicate records
Detecting and correcting errors, inconsistencies, and inaccuracies in data
Encrypting sensitive data
Compressing data to save storage space
questions.correct_answer: Detecting and correcting errors, inconsistencies, and inaccuracies in data
questions.explanation: Data cleansing (or data scrubbing) is the process of identifying and correcting or removing errors, inconsistencies, and inaccuracies in data to improve its quality.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of data governance?
options: To increase data storage capacity
To establish policies, standards, and processes for managing data as an organizational asset
To encrypt all organizational data
To reduce the number of databases in an organization
questions.correct_answer: To establish policies, standards, and processes for managing data as an organizational asset
questions.explanation: Data governance provides the framework, policies, and oversight needed to ensure data is managed effectively, securely, and in compliance with regulations while maintaining quality.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of automating data quality checks?
options: Eliminates the need for data governance
Ensures consistent, scalable, and continuous monitoring of data quality
Removes all data quality issues permanently
Makes manual data review unnecessary in all cases
questions.correct_answer: Ensures consistent, scalable, and continuous monitoring of data quality
questions.explanation: Automation enables consistent application of data quality rules, can scale to large datasets, and provides continuous monitoring. However, it doesn't eliminate the need for governance or human oversight.

questions.question: Master Data Management (MDM) primarily focuses on:
options: Managing only customer data
Creating and maintaining a single, consistent, and accurate view of critical business entities
Backing up all organizational data
Managing only transactional data
questions.correct_answer: Creating and maintaining a single, consistent, and accurate view of critical business entities
questions.explanation: MDM focuses on identifying, linking, and synchronizing master data (customers, products, suppliers, etc.) across the enterprise to create a 'golden record' or single source of truth.
questions.learning_objective: Explore the principles of master data management (MDM)

questions.question: Which of the following is typically considered master data?
options: Daily sales transactions
Customer contact information
Application log files
Email messages
questions.correct_answer: Customer contact information
questions.explanation: Master data includes core business entities like customers, products, suppliers, locations, and employees. Transaction data, logs, and emails are not master data.
questions.learning_objective: Explore the principles of master data management (MDM)

questions.question: In MDM architecture, what is a 'golden record'?
options: The oldest record in the database
A record that has never been modified
The single, most accurate and complete version of a data entity
A record stored in a secure vault
questions.correct_answer: The single, most accurate and complete version of a data entity
questions.explanation: A golden record (or master record) is the authoritative, trusted version of a master data entity, created by consolidating and reconciling data from multiple sources.
questions.learning_objective: Explore the principles of master data management (MDM)

questions.question: Which MDM implementation style maintains master data in a central hub and distributes it to operational systems?
options: Registry style
Coexistence style
Consolidation style
Centralized (or Transaction) style
questions.correct_answer: Centralized (or Transaction) style
questions.explanation: In the centralized/transaction style, master data is created and maintained in the MDM hub, which becomes the system of record and distributes data to other systems.
questions.learning_objective: Explore the principles of master data management (MDM)

questions.question: Data stewardship in the context of MDM refers to:
options: Storing data on physical servers
The responsibility for ensuring the quality, security, and proper use of data
Creating database backups
Writing SQL queries
questions.correct_answer: The responsibility for ensuring the quality, security, and proper use of data
questions.explanation: Data stewards are individuals responsible for managing, overseeing, and ensuring the quality and proper governance of specific data domains within the MDM framework.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key challenge in implementing MDM?
options: Lack of data in organizations
Resistance to change and organizational silos
Too many MDM vendor options
Insufficient storage capacity
questions.correct_answer: Resistance to change and organizational silos
questions.explanation: Cultural and organizational challenges, including resistance to change, departmental silos, and lack of cross-functional collaboration, are often the biggest barriers to successful MDM implementation.

questions.question: Data matching and deduplication in MDM involve:
options: Deleting all duplicate database tables
Identifying and merging records that represent the same real-world entity
Creating backup copies of master data
Matching data types across different systems
questions.correct_answer: Identifying and merging records that represent the same real-world entity
questions.explanation: Data matching uses algorithms to identify records from different sources that refer to the same entity, while deduplication merges or eliminates redundant records to create a single master record.

questions.question: Cloud-based MDM solutions offer which advantage over on-premises solutions?
options: Complete elimination of data security concerns
Scalability and reduced infrastructure management burden
No need for data governance
Automatic resolution of all data quality issues
questions.correct_answer: Scalability and reduced infrastructure management burden
questions.explanation: Cloud-based MDM provides scalability, faster deployment, reduced IT infrastructure costs, and easier updates, though it still requires proper governance and security measures.

questions.question: What role does data lineage play in data quality and MDM?
options: It has no relevance to data quality
It tracks data's origin, transformations, and movement through systems
It only applies to historical data
It is used solely for compliance purposes
questions.correct_answer: It tracks data's origin, transformations, and movement through systems
questions.explanation: Data lineage provides visibility into data's lifecycle—where it comes from, how it's transformed, and where it's used. This is crucial for understanding data quality issues and maintaining trust in master data.

questions.question: Which metric would best measure the completeness dimension of data quality?
options: Percentage of records with all required fields populated
Number of database queries per second
Average response time for data retrieval
Total storage capacity used
questions.correct_answer: Percentage of records with all required fields populated
questions.explanation: Completeness measures whether all required data is present. The percentage of records with populated mandatory fields is a direct measure of this dimension.
questions.learning_objective: Define data quality and its dimensions

questions.question: In the context of MDM, what is 'data harmonization'?
options: Backing up data to multiple locations
Standardizing data formats, definitions, and values across different systems
Encrypting sensitive data
Compressing data to save space
questions.correct_answer: Standardizing data formats, definitions, and values across different systems
questions.explanation: Data harmonization involves standardizing data elements across different systems so they have consistent formats, definitions, and value representations, enabling effective data integration and MDM.
questions.learning_objective: Explore the principles of master data management (MDM)

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a data quality scorecard?
options: A tool that automatically fixes all data quality issues
A visual representation of data quality metrics and KPIs over time
A ranking of employees based on data entry accuracy
A security tool for monitoring data access
questions.correct_answer: A visual representation of data quality metrics and KPIs over time
questions.explanation: A data quality scorecard provides stakeholders with a dashboard view of key data quality metrics, dimensions, and trends, helping track progress and identify areas needing improvement.
